beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Some word problems take two steps. The trick is to take them one at a time. Here is one.

do.text: Two steps, one at a time
First one step. Then the next.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A class gets five boxes with six pencils in each. It uses twenty-nine pencils. How many are left?

do.text: 5 boxes with 6 pencils in each. 29 are used. How many are left?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Thirty! Five times six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Thirty arrived. But the story keeps going. Let's make a picture that keeps both steps.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each little piece stands for one pencil. Six pieces make one box. Five equal boxes join into one strip.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five times six is thirty pencils altogether.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: We want the number left. We don't know it yet, so we give it a name: the letter *r*.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Next, the class uses twenty-nine. Take those pieces away from the whole delivery.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One piece is left! Thirty was only the first step.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Check its size: twenty-nine is almost all of thirty. We should have very little left.

do.text: Almost all used → very little left

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One pencil makes sense.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: An equation says two amounts are equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five times six

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: minus twenty-nine

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: is the number left, *r*.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is another one. Buy six notebooks at seven dollars each. Pay forty-seven dollars. How much change comes back?

do.text: 6 notebooks at 7 dollars each. You pay 47. How much change?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: About forty dollars for the notebooks, so I expect a few dollars back. The change should be much less than the payment.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six notebooks at seven dollars cost forty-two dollars. Now take forty-two away from forty-seven.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Forty-seven minus forty-two is five. Five dollars come back.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two steps again. First the whole cost. Then the change.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One more story. This time, three things happen. A shop has fifty-seven tulips. Sixteen more arrive. Then twenty-six are sold, and later twenty-one more. How many are left?

do.text: 57 tulips. 16 arrive. 26 are sold, then 21 more. How many are left?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each change needs a sign. Does it add tulips, or take them away?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Plus, minus, minus: one delivery, then two sales. First, fifty-seven plus sixteen is seventy-three.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Take away twenty-six, then twenty-one. Twenty-six tulips left.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Round to tens to check: sixty plus twenty, minus thirty, minus twenty is thirty. Twenty-six is close.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Do what happened first, then what happened next,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: and ask whether the answer is the right size.
